# Content playbook — the 6 proven formats (2026-07-07)

Source: the transcript decode — every format below produced real numbers for Surface Care /
Adam Hall / the Jim's Group content machine. Rule from Joel Kleber (took Jim's to a $1B valuation):
**volume beats polish** — post rough, post often, learn what works. Film 60 seconds on every job.
House rules apply to captions: no "written", no "guarantee", no em-dashes, claims physically true.

## Format 1 — Job story before/after (their #1, use on EVERY job)
Structure: the PROBLEM as a story → what it would have cost to replace → the fix → the reveal.
> Caption template: "Customer dropped a [thing] and chipped the [surface]. Replacement quote: $[X]
> thousand. We resurfaced it in [Y] hours for a fraction of that. [suburb], job #[n]."
Shots: 5s damage close-up → 10s masking/prep → 10s spraying → 10s peel + reveal → 5s wide.
(Surface Care's version of this is their whole grid. Real example hooks in the archiver: "Customer
dropped a jar of pistachio spread from up high and chipped the...")

## Format 2 — "We tried to damage the repair" (their 115K-view viral)
After cure, on camera: keys dragged, kettle water, scrubbing — the coating shrugs it off.
> Caption: "Resurfaced this bath last month. Today we tried to damage it. [result]. This is why
> the warranty is up to 5 years." (Only claim what the video shows.)

## Format 3 — Transparent weekly numbers (Jordan's signature)
> "This week: [X] quote requests, [Y] quotes sent, [Z] jobs booked. Here's what we learned: …"
Post even while numbers are small — "3 quotes this week" reads as honest, not weak. The Monday
brief bot produces these numbers automatically.

## Format 4 — Honest pricing breakdown
Where the money goes on a $1,050 benchtop job: materials, labour hours, travel, what we keep.
Nobody in the trade does this; it converts because it kills the "getting ripped off" fear.
(Adam Hall's whiteboard-economics posts are the model — markup vs margin, why cheap quotes lie.)

## Format 5 — The 60-second promise (speed brag)
Screen-record (redact the number) answering an enquiry inside a minute, or the ack SMS landing.
> "Most trades take 3 days to call back. Watch what happens when you message us." Their version:
> "We actually call people back, which seems to be not a thing in the construction industry."

## Format 6 — Founder build-in-public (Allan's unfair advantage)
Two mates + AI co-CEOs rebuilding a $2M playbook for bathrooms: the cockpit, the atlas, the
quote app, real decisions ("we just cut our quote validity to 7 days, here's why"). Nobody else
in Australian trades has this story. Adam Hall never posts about fencing — "people buy off
people" — and it built a $19.5M brand.

## Cadence + engine
- 3 posts/week minimum (1× Format 1 from a real job, 1× any of 2-5, 1× Format 6).
- Same clip → IG Reel + FB + (later) TikTok. Shoot vertical 9:16 once.
- Every post's comments = leads: the comment-replier flow (social-agents runbook, Agent C) DMs
  them the quote link the moment FB/IG connect to GHL.
- Swipe-file: the archivers (:8317/:8318) hold all 645 source videos transcribed + searchable —
  before writing any post, search the format for their working hook.
- Measure Jordan's way when volume grows: amplify only organic winners with paid, kill anything
  that doesn't lower cost-per-lead.
